wald: Wald Tests and Confidence Intervals

Ivan Jacob Agaloos Pesigan

Source: vignettes/wald.Rmd
wald.Rmd

Description

Wald tests and Wald confidence intervals in R (R Core Team, 2026). Each exported function has an internal version without input checks that other projects can copy.

Installation

You can install the development version of wald from GitHub with:

if (!require("pak")) install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("ijapesigan/wald")

Example 

library(package = "wald")

A linear regression model fitted to the mtcars data.

fit <- stats::lm(
  formula = mpg ~ wt + hp,
  data = datasets::mtcars
)

Tests and Confidence Intervals for Each Parameter

CIWald() tests each parameter against theta and gives Wald confidence intervals from the t distribution (z = FALSE) or the standard normal distribution (z = TRUE).

CIWald(
  est = stats::coef(object = fit),
  se = sqrt(x = diag(x = stats::vcov(object = fit))),
  theta = 0,
  alpha = c(0.05, 0.01),
  z = FALSE,
  df = stats::df.residual(object = fit)
)
#>                     est         se         t df            p        0.5%
#> (Intercept) 37.22727012 1.59878754 23.284689 29 2.565459e-20 32.82039468
#> wt          -3.87783074 0.63273349 -6.128695 29 1.119647e-06 -5.62188843
#> hp          -0.03177295 0.00902971 -3.518712 29 1.451229e-03 -0.05666231
#>                    2.5%       97.5%        99.5%
#> (Intercept) 33.95738245 40.49715778 41.634145549
#> wt          -5.17191604 -2.58374544 -2.133773058
#> hp          -0.05024078 -0.01330512 -0.006883583

With test = TRUE, only the tests are returned.

CIWald(
  est = stats::coef(object = fit),
  se = sqrt(x = diag(x = stats::vcov(object = fit))),
  z = TRUE,
  test = TRUE
)
#>                     est         se         z             p
#> (Intercept) 37.22727012 1.59878754 23.284689 6.337117e-120
#> wt          -3.87783074 0.63273349 -6.128695  8.860267e-10
#> hp          -0.03177295 0.00902971 -3.518712  4.336473e-04

Joint Test of the Slopes

Wald() tests the null hypothesis that a vector of parameters equals theta (zeros when theta = NULL), from the \chi^{2} distribution.

slopes <- c("wt", "hp")
Wald(
  est = stats::coef(object = fit)[slopes],
  var_est = stats::vcov(object = fit)[slopes, slopes],
  theta = NULL
)
#>        chisq           df            p 
#> 1.384224e+02 2.000000e+00 8.748869e-31

Probabilities of Significance Levels

ProbsofAlpha() returns the tail probabilities that define two-sided intervals.

ProbsofAlpha(alpha = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001))
#> [1] 0.0005 0.0050 0.0250 0.9750 0.9950 0.9995
